Checked the original Caravenna–Daneri SISSA preprint 24/2009/M, §3.1, Definitions 3.1–3.2, Theorem 3.3 (3.5)–(3.6), and §4.7. The theorem is for a real-valued convex function on all of Euclidean space, Lebesgue measure restricted to a finite-measure set, and the gradient partition on a σ-compact full-Lebesgue-measure differentiability domain with convex fibers. It gives mutual absolute continuity with intrinsic Hausdorff measure on the projected fiber intersected with the restriction set, for gradient-marginal-a.e. slope. The argument uses this projected theorem and the actual graph-area formula; it does not use the dimension wording of Remark 3.5 or require the theorem at any fixed null slope.

The differentiability set is Borel and admits compact exhaustion up to an ambient null set. The gradient restricted to it is continuous by local boundedness and closedness of the subgradient graph. The saturated sets are compact images for fixed original compact set, parameter 1/j and closed ball for z, because ∇f(q)∈∂f(z) is a closed condition there. The saturation is thus σ-compact and includes the original full-measure union.

At tq+(1−t)z, t>0, equality on the affine contact segment makes every supporting slope at that point a supporting slope at the differentiability point q; hence the new point has gradient p. Each retained fiber contains ri C(p) by extending from an original q across any chosen relative-interior point, then choosing a sufficiently small reciprocal-integer coefficient. A convex combination of two retained points still retains a positive coefficient of one original q, reducible to some 1/j by absorbing the excess into a convex combination inside C(p). This gives a convex fiber of dimension dim aff C(p); the omitted subset of C(p) lies on its intrinsically null relative boundary, with empty relative boundary in dimension zero.

At a boundary point, choosing the vertical axis toward an interior ball gives an interior point of the projected domain and positive separation of upper and lower graphs nearby. The lower convex graph on an open ball is a relatively open boundary patch. Extending it by the supremum of its supporting affine functions on a slightly larger compactly contained ball gives a globally finite convex Lipschitz function: both slopes and intercepts are bounded there, and its supporting functions realize the original value on that larger ball. The local bounded open V is Borel and of finite Lebesgue measure, so all hypotheses of the theorem apply.

The graph area formula weights by J(p)=sqrt(1+|p|²), a positive finite function constant on each gradient fiber. It only reweights the gradient marginal, preserving both its null sets and the probability conditionals. The slope-to-normal map is a homeomorphism onto the downward hemisphere. A tangent plane supporting the local body supports the whole convex body, since a segment from the contact point to a violator would violate it arbitrarily locally. The plane-contact equation on the patch is exactly the lift of C(p)∩V. This meets the relative interior of the projected contact set and has its full dimension, while the relatively open patch meeting the physical face likewise has that face’s full dimension. The affine lift has the claimed positive k-Jacobian (one for k=0) and preserves the intrinsic Hausdorff measure class.

For each patch the marginal is c_jσ with c_j=η_u(P_j), and its conditional is η_u|P_j/c_j where c_j>0. A null set for c_jσ is σ-null on {c_j>0}; countably many patches therefore give one σ-conull good set. A positive-mass patch must meet the relative interior by local equivalence and relative-boundary nullity. Overlap in the relative interior of a positive and another patch is relatively open with positive intrinsic measure, making the other patch positive too. The unions of positive and zero-mass patches cannot disconnect the convex relative interior. The positive patches cover it; their countable local equivalences and intrinsic relative-boundary nullity give both directions of global equivalence. Every face neighborhood meets the relative interior in positive intrinsic measure, giving the claimed closed support. A facet normal is an atom with normalized facet area; the two interval atoms are immediate.

Under λ the multiplier dσ/dλ preserves the conclusions on its positivity set modulo λ and the kernel is zero elsewhere. ξ≤cη implies its normal marginal is λ-dominated. For every boundary set in a countable Borel generating algebra and every normal test set, the scalar inequality follows by applying ξ≤cη to the intersection with the inverse image of the test set. Taking one conull set and extending the finite-measure inequalities by monotone class proves simultaneous kernel domination.

overlap.comparison: The accepted proof shares the Borel normal and exposed-face support geometry for already-given martingale rows. It does not identify conditional measures of full surface area with intrinsic Hausdorff measure or prove reverse absolute continuity.

The accepted compact martingale lemma assumes marked measures concentrated on a common Borel graph and concludes parameter-preserving couplings. It supplies no intrinsic measure class on normal fibers.
